svg.title: Layers you own, a lifecycle you run, capabilities you add
svg.desc: On the left, a building of fourteen floors shows the layers you own. They run from infrastructure and compute (R01) at the bottom to agent data engineering (R14) at the top. In the centre, seven bands show the capabilities you add. Each band names industry products and the layers that build it. Runtime: R01 and R07. Tool gateway: R03, R04 and R05. Knowledge and memory: R02 and R14. Identity and policy: R10, R11 and R07. Evaluation and release: R06 and R12. Observability and audit trail: R12 and R11. Human oversight: R13, R08 and R09. On the right, the nine lifecycle stages run in order, and each change loops back to evaluate. Lines link each stage to the capabilities it calls on. Register, entitle and retire call on identity and policy. Sponsor and owner calls on human oversight. Evaluate and change call on evaluation and release. Approve calls on human oversight and on identity and policy. Operate calls on the runtime, the tool gateway, knowledge and memory, and observability. Periodic review calls on observability and on human oversight. A strip at the bottom gives the two rules. Policy is enforced outside the model. The audit trail is written where the agent cannot touch it.
svg.text: Layers you own, a lifecycle you run, capabilities you add
The capabilities are built across the layers. Each lifecycle stage calls on the ones it needs.
Chips: the layers that build it
AWS AgentCore Runtime, Google Agent Runtime
AWS AgentCore Gateway, Google Agent Gateway
AWS AgentCore Memory, Google Memory Bank
AgentCore Identity and Policy, Entra Agent ID
AgentCore Observability, EU AI Act Article 12
EU AI Act Article 14, sponsor and owner
Policy is enforced outside the model. The gateway and the policy decision point check every action.
The audit trail is written where the agent cannot touch it. A separate channel collects it as the work happens.
